messages: marina: Quick question — thinking about a new private-offer structure for cloud marketplace and appliance partners. Idea: tiered commit with a 3-month soft-landing (usage credit burn + reduced overage) to reduce churn at renewal. Thoughts? :thinking:
simon: sounds useful. can you sketch the economics? i.e., how much credit vs discount vs SKU uplift we need to hit a conservative ARR target

marina: high level: 1) 12m commit baseline 2) months 1-3 "soft landing" where 25% of committed $ is available as burnable credit for on-ramp 3) months 4-12 standard usage against commit. renewal window gets a small loyalty discount if commit >=90% used
jana: two quick concerns: SI integration timelines (most SI projects take 6-9 months) and marketplace listing lead times. soft-landing should align with SI go-live not just calendar months
marina: agree. plan is to make the soft-landing window flexible — machine-readable in the private-offer payload so we can set start_date = partner_go_live if needed
eric: pinging @linda-sales — will field teams be ok with credits vs straight % off? credits are easier for appliance/hardware bundles but sales prefers headline % off
linda-sales: sales prefers simple messaging ("X% off for first year + onboarding credits"). we can hide mechanics in legal/ops but PR should be a percent. also need CLAs for SIs if partner co-sell

simon: on the ops side, need these items in the private-offer metadata: commit_amount, soft_landing_percent, soft_landing_duration_days, start_trigger (manual|go_live|billing_date). simple JSON schema helps downstream automation

marina: proposed payload snippet:
```
{
  "commit_amount": "500000",
  "soft_landing_percent": "25",
  "soft_landing_duration_days": "90",
  "start_trigger": "si_go_live"
}
```

ops-bot: Reminder: private-offer lifecycle must include a scheduled auto-reconcile job and a fallback plan to hosted SKU if commit is underspent. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/marketplace-reconcile
jana: for SI contracts we should allow a 6mo extended soft-landing option for systems-integration-heavy customers. otherwise they might never hit commit and churn early
eric: agree. propose three presets: "onramp" (90d), "integration" (180d), "appliance" (120d) with configurable credit % per preset
linda-sales: question on renewals — loyalty discount only if commit >=90% OR if customer consumed >=80% and has growth plan? we want to avoid punishing customers who are expanding but under-committed
marina: good call. propose renewal rule: grant loyalty discount if (commit_utilization >=90%) OR (usage_growth_rate_last_90d >=15%). that should capture expansion
simon: need to quantify discount bands in $ terms and compute NPV impact for partner revenue share. i'll run a simulation if you give assumed uplift numbers
marina: i'll pull a salon-case with 3 example customers (SI slow, SaaS quick, appliance mid) and drop numbers tomorrow. then we can mock partner-facing copy for PR
linda-sales: ok. also need a short legal checklist: private-offer template, SI co-sell addendum, appliance warranty clause. @legal, when you see this can you flag anything we miss? :eyes:
legal: noted. please tag with example customer names and commit amounts when available. special attention to data residency obligations on appliance offers

marina: next steps: simon will prototype pricing sims, jana will map SI timelines, linda will draft high-level percent messaging, i'll draft private-offer payload and ops checklist. sync early tomorrow 9:30 PT? :+1:
linda-sales: 9:30 works for me
simon: added to my calendar
jana: 👍
marina: thanks everyone — will post the docs in the partnership drive and link here before the sync
